lesson.title: Hello & Goodbye
lesson.summary: Rita practises saying hello, asking How are you?, answering, and saying goodbye at different times of day.

objectives.text: Greet Rita and ask how she is
objectives.criteria: The learner says a greeting (hello / hi / good morning ...) and asks How are you?
check_prompts: Imagine you meet me in the morning. What do you say?

objectives.criteria: The learner answers with a phrase like I'm fine, thank you.
The learner says goodbye / see you later / good night.
check_prompts: It is late and you are going home. What do you say?

steps: Greet the learner with the right greeting for the time of day and ask: How are you?
Teach hello / hi and good morning, good afternoon, good evening with the time of day each one fits
Teach How are you? and the answers I'm fine, thank you
Teach goodbye, see you later and good night
Role-play meeting in the morning, then saying goodbye in the evening
Swap roles so the learner starts the greeting
Ask each objective's question and wait
Praise one thing the learner did well
Say one sentence that sums up the lesson

plan.teacher_notes: Good evening is for meeting someone; good night is for leaving or going to bed, and learners often swap them. Arabic uses مساء الخير for both afternoon and evening. If the learner answers in Arabic, give the English and ask them to repeat it.

lesson.title: Me & You
lesson.summary: Rita helps the learner introduce themselves: name, country, city, age and job, and ask the same questions back.

objectives.criteria: The learner says My name is ... or I'm ...
The learner says I'm from ... or I live in ...

objectives.text: Ask Rita a question about her
objectives.criteria: The learner asks a question like What's your name? / Where are you from? / How old are you?
check_prompts: Now you ask me a question.

steps: Say: My name is Rita. I'm from Jordan. Then ask: What's your name?
Model the three sentences: My name is ... / I'm from ... / I'm ... years old
Teach the matching questions: What's your name? Where are you from? How old are you?
Interview the learner with the three questions
Swap roles: the learner interviews Rita
Add friend, student, teacher or family: This is my friend, Ali.
Ask each objective's question and wait
Praise one thing the learner did well
Say one sentence that sums up the lesson

plan.teacher_notes: Learners often say 'My age is 20' or 'I have 20 years'. Model 'I'm twenty years old.' Remember I am / I'm: learners drop it (I from Jordan).

vocabulary.example: I live in a big city.
How old are you? — I'm twenty.

lesson.image_prompt: A friendly cartoon character showing 'Me & You'

lesson.title: Thank you & Please
lesson.summary: Rita practises please, thank you, sorry, excuse me and the replies you're welcome and no problem.

objectives.criteria: The learner asks for something using please (e.g. A glass of water, please / Can I ..., please?).
check_prompts: You are thirsty in a café. Ask for water.

objectives.criteria: The learner says thank you or thanks.
check_prompts: I give you a gift. What do you say?

objectives.criteria: The learner replies with You're welcome / No problem.
check_prompts: Thank you for your help! What do you say back?

steps: Set the scene: you are in a café. Say: Hello! What would you like?
Teach please at the end of a request: A glass of water, please.
Teach thank you / thanks and the replies you're welcome / no problem
Teach sorry (for a mistake) and excuse me (to get attention or to pass)
Role-play ordering in a café, swapping roles
Practise Can I ...? and Of course
Say 'Pardon?' when the learner speaks too fast so they ask you to repeat
Ask each objective's question and wait
Praise one thing the learner did well
Say one sentence that sums up the lesson

plan.teacher_notes: Thanks is informal; thank you is safe everywhere. Learners mix up sorry (a mistake) and excuse me (getting attention). Keep the tone warm and polite.

vocabulary.example: Excuse me, where is the bank?
Can you help me? — Of course.
Pardon? Can you say it again?

lesson.image_prompt: A friendly cartoon character showing 'Thank you & Please'

lesson.title: Yes, No & Great idea!
lesson.summary: Rita practises answering with yes, no, maybe and sure, suggesting with Let's ... and replying Great idea!

objectives.text: Answer a question with yes or no and a short reason
objectives.criteria: The learner answers a yes/no question with yes or no plus a few more words.
The learner says a suggestion starting with Let's (e.g. Let's play football).
check_prompts: It is the weekend. What can we do together?

objectives.text: React with Great idea! or I agree
objectives.criteria: The learner replies to a suggestion with Great idea!, I agree, sure or OK.
check_prompts: Let's eat pizza tonight! What do you say?

steps: Ask three quick questions: Do you like tea? Are you ready? Is it Friday?
Teach yes / no / maybe and short answers: Yes, I do. / No, I don't. / Yes, I am.
Teach suggestions with Let's ... and the replies Great idea!, I agree, Sure, OK
Rita suggests an activity; the learner answers with Great idea! or Maybe later
Swap: the learner suggests with Let's ... and Rita reacts
Add right / wrong when you correct something
Ask each objective's question and wait
Praise one thing the learner did well
Say one sentence that sums up the lesson

plan.teacher_notes: Learners often answer Do you like ...? with 'Yes, I like'. Model the short answer 'Yes, I do.' Encourage more than a bare yes or no.

lesson.title: I'm busy
lesson.summary: Rita practises saying how you feel and whether you are busy or free: tired, happy, hungry, ready, late.

objectives.criteria: The learner says I'm + a feeling word (tired, happy, hungry, sad, bored ...).
check_prompts: How do you feel right now?

objectives.text: Say if they are busy or free
objectives.text_ar: يقول إن كان مشغولاً أو متفرغاً
objectives.criteria: The learner says I'm busy or I'm free (with a time if possible).
The learner says something like Sorry, I'm busy now. Talk to you later.
check_prompts: Let's talk now! (You are busy.) What do you say?

steps: Ask: How do you feel today? Are you busy or free?
Teach feeling words with I'm: tired, happy, sad, hungry, thirsty, bored, ready
Teach busy / free and the polite postpone: Sorry, I'm busy now. Talk to you later.
Mime a feeling and let the learner guess: Are you tired?
Role-play a friend inviting the learner while they are busy
Ask: Are you free on Friday?
Ask each objective's question and wait
Praise one thing the learner did well
Say one sentence that sums up the lesson

plan.teacher_notes: Feelings use I'm + the word (I'm tired). Learners drop I'm (I busy): model the full sentence. Free here means 'not busy', not 'costing nothing'.

vocabulary.example: I'm busy. Talk to you later.

lesson.image_prompt: A friendly cartoon character showing 'I'm busy'
